H&P – Super Detailed Clinical Note  

Consult Summary:  
Two-day history of gradually worsening constant burning suprapubic abdominal pain with subjective fever/diaphoresis, increased urinary frequency, and pink-tinged urine in an otherwise healthy reproductive-age woman; empirically treated as uncomplicated cystitis with trimethoprim, advised pregnancy test and close follow-up.

History:  
• Presenting complaint: Constant burning pain “below my belly button,” started ~48 h ago, gradually worsening.  
• Associated symptoms:  
  – Subjective feeling “hot and sweaty” (no documented temperature).  
  – Mild nausea; no vomiting.  
  – ↑ Urinary frequency; urine noted “a little pink” (possible hematuria).  
  – No dysuria, no flank pain.  
  – Bowels: constipation last week (resolved); currently normal; no diarrhea.  
  – No respiratory, cardiac, neurologic, or visual symptoms.  
• Gynecologic/sexual review: Sexually active with one partner, last intercourse 4 days ago. Implanon inserted 1 yr ago; still menstruating. Last menstrual period ≈2 weeks ago. No vaginal bleeding or discharge.  
• Timeline: Symptoms began 2 days ago → gradually intensifying; no prior similar episodes.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: None identified.  
• Pertinent negatives: No dysuria, vomiting, dyspareunia, cough, SOB, palpitations, headaches.

Past Medical History:  
• No chronic medical conditions reported.  
• Surgical history: None.  
• Obstetric/gynecologic: Implanon in situ (1 yr). No prior ectopic or PID noted.  
• Medications:  
  – Etonogestrel implant (Implanon) – dose/route/frequency not applicable.  
  – Newly prescribed: Trimethoprim 1 tablet twice daily for 3 days.  
  – PRN advice: Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• Allergies: Not documented.  ❖

Social History:  
• Lives in a share-house with two roommates.  
• Occupation: Accountant.  
• Tobacco: Non-smoker.  
• Alcohol: Social use, “not more than normal.”  
• Recreational drugs: Not mentioned.

Family History:  
• Denies relevant familial gastrointestinal or genitourinary disorders.

Physical Examination:  
• Telehealth visit – no vitals or physical findings recorded.

Investigations:  
• None obtained. Urine culture/urinalysis and pregnancy test discussed but deferred by patient (home pregnancy test advised).

Assessment & Plan:  
Issue 1 – Suprapubic pain with hematuria, likely acute uncomplicated cystitis  
• Empiric antibiotics: Trimethoprim 1 tablet BID × 3 days (e-script sent).  
• Symptomatic care: Paracetamol for pain; encourage hydration and cranberry juice.  
• Safety-net: Return if pain worsens, fever develops, vomiting, rigors, or symptoms persist beyond treatment course.

Issue 2 – Rule-out pregnancy/ectopic pregnancy  
• Counselled on very low but present risk with Implanon.  
• Advised home urine pregnancy test today; repeat or seek care if positive or if new vaginal bleeding, dizziness, or severe pain.

Issue 3 – Diagnostic clarification / follow-up  
• If no improvement in a few days, will arrange:  
  – Urinalysis ± culture.  
  – Serum β-hCG if pregnancy status unclear.  
  – Further abdominal/pelvic evaluation (exam, labs, imaging) to exclude appendicitis, PID, or other causes.  
• Follow-up: Televisit or in-person review in 3–5 days or sooner if deterioration.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):  
1. Acute cystitis – High likelihood: classic suprapubic pain, urinary frequency, possible hematuria, mild systemic features.  
2. Acute appendicitis – Moderate likelihood: peri-umbilical pain with gradual worsening, mild nausea; absent RLQ localization currently.  
3. Ectopic pregnancy – Low-moderate likelihood: reproductive age, lower-abd pain; Implanon and recent period make it less probable but must be excluded.  
(Other DDx such as PID or renal stone considered low based on history.)

Quality checks:  
● Missing but expected: Allergies, complete medication reconciliation, vital signs, physical examination, urinalysis, pregnancy test.  
● Conflicts: Patient name alternates between “Tim” and “Kim” (conflict noted).  
● Transcript quality: Clear overall; minor conversational noise but clinically adequate.
